status_summary: On 2026-06-26 HHS sent termination letters to 53 of 67 Teen Pregnancy Prevention grantees, about 68 million dollars, citing misalignment with agency priorities, with one letter saying the program normalized or promoted sexual activity by minors. HHS posted a 63.4 million dollar funding opportunity on 2026-06-23 to replicate effective programs (applications due 2026-07-23) and an 8.3 million dollar evaluation opportunity. The replication notice requires sexual risk avoidance education and promotion of delayed sexual initiation, advance parent notice, review of materials and opt-out, alignment with agency priorities, and program eligibility under stated criteria rather than a named list. No lawsuit over the terminations was reported as of late June 2026.

timeline.event: Office of Population Affairs posts the Replicating Effective Teen Pregnancy Prevention Programs funding opportunity (63.4 million dollars, about 52 awards), requiring sexual risk avoidance education and parent notice and opt-out.
HHS terminates 53 of 67 Teen Pregnancy Prevention grants worth about 68 million dollars; new funding opportunities require an alignment review.

title: Redirect the Teen Pregnancy Prevention program toward sexual risk avoidance
uncertainties: The terminations rest on one news report; the termination letters were not read. Whether awards were made under the new opportunities by the end of fiscal year 2026 was not confirmed, and the evaluation opportunity was not opened. The replication notice's Appendix A criteria and conscience section were not fully visible. PREP and funding parity were not examined.
